body.heading: A community is a team
paragraphs: No one does everything. A community works because different people do different jobs — growing food, teaching children, fixing pipes, healing hurts — and trade the results with each other.
Here are ten of the helpers around you. Notice how many of them you have already met this week!

body.heading: People who help us learn and heal
paragraphs: A teacher helps children learn new things and ask better questions.
A doctor finds out why your body hurts and how to fix it. A nurse cares for patients every day and helps the doctor.
A librarian guards a building full of stories and helps you find the exact book you need.

body.heading: People who feed and build
paragraphs: A farmer grows food — vegetables, fruit, grain — and cares for animals.
A baker turns flour, water and yeast into bread, rolls and cakes, starting work before the sun is up.
A builder constructs houses, schools and bridges from plans, wood, stone and steel.
A plumber fixes pipes so clean water comes in and dirty water goes away. An electrician makes sure lights and machines get power safely.

body.heading: People who protect
paragraphs: A firefighter races to fires, rescues people and teaches everyone how to stay safe.
A police officer helps keep people safe, directs traffic and helps when there is an emergency.
Every one of these jobs exists because someone, long ago, said: 'People need this. I will learn to do it well.'

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Count how many of these helpers your family has relied on this month. Did the number surprise you?
2. Invent a job that does not exist yet but should. What problem would it solve, and what would its day look like?

takeaway: Jobs are how a community shares work — teachers, nurses, farmers, bakers, builders, firefighters and more, each doing a part nobody could do alone.
